title: filter_rows: keep rows that satisfy a condition
description: Keep only rows that satisfy a condition on a single column. Removes all rows that do not match. Supports numeric comparisons (>, >=, <, <=, =, !=), string equality, and missing-value checks with is_null or is_not_null. Use this when the user wants to focus on a subset of data, such as rows above a threshold, matching a category, or rows where a column is missing.

parameters.name: column
parameters.description: The column to apply the filter condition to. Must exist in the dataset.

parameters.name: operator
parameters.description: Comparison operator. Allowed values (use exactly): = (equal), != (not equal), > (greater than), >= (greater than or equal), < (less than), <= (less than or equal), is_null (missing values), is_not_null (non-missing values). Do NOT use 'equals', 'eq', 'gt', 'gte', 'lt', 'lte', 'missing', or any other form.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The value to compare against. Required for =, !=, >, >=, <, and <=. Omit this field for is_null and is_not_null.

rag_note: Filtering may produce zero rows if the condition matches nothing. The executor will raise an empty_output warning in that case. If the user asks to filter by a column that does not exist, the validator will reject the workflow.
